doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: Learning to improvise and the chord changes
summary: He didn't realize improvising was happening at first and explains that players improvise off chord changes, not the melody.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: How did that work for you? Did you stumble into improvising because it was required or did you really seek it out beforehand?

The one and the same. It was part of it you know. As a matter of fact, I didn’t know it was improvising, like with “Bags’ Groove” like when Miles said [scats] you know? I didn’t know that was necessarily improvised. As a matter of fact, I hadn’t really seen a lead sheet until after I had read “Infant Eyes” you know. You know it was just playing and then after a while you realized they was soloing. Because see most people, they don’t improvise off the song anyway. They improvise off the chord changes. For instance like

he said, “Well let’s play ‘Straight, No Chaser.’” You say okay. Well “Straight, No Chaser” is a blues you know. So you play “Straight, No Chaser” and when the solos start, you know, they might as well be playing “Every Day I Have the Blues” or anything you know, but they’re not improvising off “Straight, No Chaser” because see if you was improvising off “Straight, No Chaser” you’d say [scats] you know like the melody [scats]. You know what I mean?
Yeah like you almost turned it upside down.

Yeah you improvise off the melody and the chords, but they just improvise off the chords. This is why they could steal each other’s music with the same chord changes. Like take “Indiana” and make it “Donna Lee.” You understand what I’m saying?
